precepts.text: Sychar was near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph; a parcel of land and an inheritance are one and the same.
precepts.point: Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and purchased Ruth to be his wife to raise up the name of the dead, that it be not cut off from among his brethren.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Ruth 4 is a trial at the gate before ten elders over land. Elimelech had land; he died, and his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died too, leaving no man to take it. So the land had to be taken up by the next of kin. Boaz told the nearer kinsman that Naomi “selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.” A parcel of land: that phrase opens the whole chapter.

John 4 uses the same wording. Christ “must needs go through Samaria. Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Jacob gave Joseph that parcel of ground; he bought his son that land.

A parcel of land, a parcel of ground, a parcel of a field: they are all the same thing, and a parcel of land and an inheritance are one and the same. So when Boaz bought the parcel that was Elimelech's, he was not making an ordinary purchase. He was taking up an inheritance in Israel, one that had to stay in the family of the dead.

precepts.text: Jacob bought a parcel of a field at Shechem from the children of Hamor for a hundred pieces of money; the field was bought before his sons ever took it by the sword.
precepts.point: Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and purchased Ruth to be his wife to raise up the name of the dead, that it be not cut off from among his brethren.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Genesis 33 gives the history behind the “parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph” in John 4. “Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan–aram; and pitched his tent before the city. And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for an hundred pieces of money.”

Jacob bought that land from the Hamites for a hundred pieces of money, and “he erected there an altar, and called it El–elohe–Israel.” A parcel of a field is again the same thing as a parcel of land: an inheritance.

Later, as he was dying, Israel told Joseph, “Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.” His sons did take the land by the sword; Simeon and Levi went crazy and killed the men of that city. But the field was bought first, before his sons ever took it. So the inheritance at Shechem stood on a lawful purchase, the same way Boaz bought Elimelech's parcel before the elders at the gate.

precepts.text: Joseph's bones were buried in that parcel of ground at Shechem, and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph; the parcel of ground is the land of inheritance.
precepts.point: Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and purchased Ruth to be his wife to raise up the name of the dead, that it be not cut off from among his brethren.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
“And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.” The parcel of ground, the parcel of land, the parcel of a field is the land of inheritance, and this one was given to Ephraim.

That is what Boaz was protecting in Ruth 4. The nearer kinsman would not redeem it, “lest I mar mine own inheritance”, and plucked off his shoe; here the shoe is passed without shame, because he is yielding the right to someone else, not refusing his brother. Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and took Ruth, the wife of Mahlon, “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren.” The son he raised up would inherit that land, because it belonged to Mahlon. Boaz is still the father; Boaz begat Obed, and the line goes through Boaz. There are no two fathers. The land falls under the dead man's line; the lineage goes back to Boaz. That is love your neighbor as yourself.

So Elimelech did not lose his land. We kept our land in house. Land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your children; don't sell it off. Our people once had millions of acres in America, and Esau made laws, eminent domain among them, and found a distant kin to pay off with a little money, and so stole millions of acres, beaches included, from Judah.

The allotment still stands. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land, and Judges says “the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” Those families are here today. The Lord says he “will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” Whoever is left after the destruction, those who repent, will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

precepts.text: The Lord will bring them again, every man to his heritage and every man to his land; every family was allotted land when we came out of Egypt, and the families that remain will be given it back when he returns.
precepts.point: The genealogy follows Boaz, the land follows Mahlon and Elimelech: you inherit land, you do not inherit a tribe, and here both were Judah anyway.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
“And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed”. Boaz raised up seed in the name of Mahlon, but the record says Boaz begat Obed, not Mahlon, because Mahlon was dead. The genealogy goes under Boaz; the land falls under the dead man's line. Obed takes on the land of Elimelech even though that is not his father's line. That is the inheritance: the parcel of land, the parcel of field, the parcel of ground. You don't inherit a tribe; you inherit the land. And they were both of the same tribe anyway.

That is why the scripture says this in Jeremiah: “And it shall come to pass, after that I have plucked them out I will return, and have compassion on them, and will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” It literally means what it says. In the beginning God allotted every family land.

The line of David had an inheritance given to it; the families of Judah each had land appointed to them. Guess what? Those families are here today. When the Lord returns, those that make it, that repented, are going back to that land, every man to his heritage.

That is why Boaz raised up seed for Elimelech's family: so the land would stay within that family's inheritance. That is loving your neighbor as yourself. We kept our land in house. So land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your kids; don't just sell it off. A lot of Judah had millions of acres here in America, and Esau stole them, creating laws like eminent domain and finding some distant kin to pay a little money and take the land. There are beaches that belong to us. But the Lord will bring every man again to his heritage and to his land.

precepts.text: When Joshua let the people go, every man went unto his inheritance to possess the land; every family had land and an inheritance, and it belongs to the men, with the wives benefiting as Eve did from Adam.
precepts.point: The genealogy follows Boaz, the land follows Mahlon and Elimelech: you inherit land, you do not inherit a tribe, and here both were Judah anyway.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Judges shows how the land was first given: “And when Joshua had let the people go, the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” We all had land and an inheritance. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land. Whoever of those same families is left after the destruction takes place will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

Notice it says every man unto his inheritance. Sisters, you're divorcing us and taking half our stuff, but it says every man. Our wives benefit from our inheritance; it belongs to the men, but it is theirs too because they are married to us. According to God, the inheritance belongs to the men, just as the earth belonged to Adam, and Eve benefitted from it because she was helping him.

And the land we inherit is not an acre or something. 1 Chronicles 2 shows Jair “who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead”, “even threescore cities”. We owned cities. Somebody literally owned the Bronx, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens. We had castles on those cities, winter houses and summer houses.

That is why the land in Ruth had to stay with Elimelech's family. Boaz begat Obed, and the genealogy goes through Boaz down to Jesse and David, but the inheritance, every man's portion from the time of Joshua, stayed with the dead man's line through the seed raised up to him.

precepts.text: When Boaz went in unto Ruth the Lord gave her conception; that is how conception happens, and the Lord gave it.
precepts.point: Thy cousin Elisabeth hath also conceived a son in her old age, for with God nothing shall be impossible; also means the same way, and the impossible thing is a barren old woman bearing, not a birth without a father.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Gabriel tells Mary, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”. It is the same word used of her cousin: “And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived”. What does it mean to conceive? To conceive you need seed; the man’s seed has to go in and fertilize the egg. Some might be confused, so Ruth shows how that happens.

“So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.” When Boaz went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception. That is how it works: a husband goes in unto his wife, and the Lord gives the conception.

And when Luke 1:28 says the angel “came in unto her”, he came in and talked with her. He did not come in and have sex with her; he came in and talked to her, plain and simple. So when Luke 1:31 says Mary shall conceive, it is conception the way Ruth conceived, the Lord giving it when her husband came unto her. It could well have been the first time Joseph touched her that the Lord made her conceive.

precepts.text: The nearer kinsman could not redeem it, lest he mar his own inheritance, and the right passed to Boaz.
precepts.point: The man who refused was called before the elders; his brother's wife loosed his shoe from off his foot, spat in his face, and answered, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house; and his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.

note.label: Deuteronomy 25: Just Judgment, the Brother's Duty, and Amalek

precepts.why:
Boaz went up to the gate, where this law sends the matter, and “took ten men of the elders of the city”. He said to the nearer kinsman: “Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s”, and “If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it”. The kinsman said, “I will redeem it.”

“Then said Boaz, What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. And the kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself; for I cannot redeem it.” The nearer kinsman could not redeem it, lest he mar his own inheritance, and the right passed to Boaz.

Here is what the law stood for: raising up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. The name was not to be put out of Israel because of the land inheritance, and the wife of the dead and the field went together. Check this out: this is no longer the law, so do not try to use it as an excuse toward your brother's wife.

precepts.text: Reading ahead for understanding: whoever bought the field of Naomi had to buy it also of Ruth, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.
precepts.point: The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Reading ahead for understanding: “What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.”

Behind the words the wife of the dead stands the law of the husband's brother. Whoever bought the field of Naomi had to take Ruth, the wife of the dead, with it, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. That is the rest in the house of her husband that Naomi wished for her daughters in law: an inheritance, and a name kept in the earth.

precepts.text: The chief fathers of Gilead brought the case of the daughters of Zelophehad: if the daughters married into another tribe, their inheritance would be taken from the inheritance of the fathers and put to the tribe wherein they were received, and fixed there at the jubile.
precepts.point: What is this going back to? The law of the land, the law of inheritance when it comes to land, read back in the book of Numbers. The husband died and the two sons died, and the only person left is the wife with the land; so she instinctively went to Boaz, and Boaz is now conducting the laws of the land of who it should be passed down to, going down the list of inheritance.
precepts.why:
Boaz is conducting the laws of the land, going down the list of who the inheritance should be passed to, and that goes back to the law of land inheritance in Numbers. “And the chief fathers of the families of the children of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of the sons of Joseph, came near, and spake before Moses, and before the princes, the chief fathers of the children of Israel”.

They brought the case of the daughters of Zelophehad: “The Lord commanded my lord to give the land for an inheritance by lot to the children of Israel: and my lord was commanded by the Lord to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother unto his daughters. And if they be married to any of the sons of the other tribes of the children of Israel, then shall their inheritance be taken from the inheritance of our fathers, and shall be put to the inheritance of the tribe whereunto they are received”. And at the jubile it would be fixed there, taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of their fathers.

Reading between the lines, you were able to marry outside your particular tribe. You can be Judah and marry somebody from Manasseh, or Manasseh and marry somebody from Ephraim; that is why they had this complaint in the first place. It just has to be within the twelve tribes of Israel, inside your nation, not outside with the heathen. Elimelech's husband and sons died and only Naomi was left with the land, so she instinctively went to Boaz, and he is now applying this law.

precepts.text: The answer: let them marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father, so that no inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe.
precepts.point: What is this going back to? The law of the land, the law of inheritance when it comes to land, read back in the book of Numbers. The husband died and the two sons died, and the only person left is the wife with the land; so she instinctively went to Boaz, and Boaz is now conducting the laws of the land of who it should be passed down to, going down the list of inheritance.
precepts.why:
The answer given through Moses: “The tribe of the sons of Joseph hath said well. This is the thing which the Lord doth command concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, Let them marry to whom they think best; only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.”

“So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe: for every one of the children of Israel shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.” Every daughter that possessed an inheritance was to be wife to one of the family of the tribe of her father, “that the children of Israel may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.”

That is the law of the land Boaz is going by. The land which was our brother Elimelech's must stay with the family, so Boaz goes down the list: the nearer kinsman first, and I am after thee. Marrying outside the tribe was fine within the twelve tribes of Israel; the point of the law is that the inheritance does not remove from tribe to tribe, and never goes outside the nation.

precepts.text: The wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother shall take her to wife, and the firstborn shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.
precepts.point: What law is that going back to? That law goes back to Deuteronomy 25, the duty of the husband's brother: the widow of the dead does not marry without unto a stranger, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. This law was taught in full when it was read ahead at Ruth 1:6-9 in these notes: the firstborn carries the weight of the name, and the shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house.
precepts.why:
Whoever took the land had to take the dead brother's wife with it; Ruth the Moabitess came along as a parcel of the land, to keep the name of Mahlon alive. That goes back to the duty of the husband's brother. “If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband’s brother unto her.”

“And it shall be, that the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.” That is what Boaz means by raising up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.

Notice the bottom of verse 5: upon his inheritance. This law applies to inheritance; it went into the law of land being passed down. It does not apply today. Your husband dying does not mean his brother now has to go in unto you and raise up children, because that duty was due to the law of inheritance, and Israel has no land inheritance in this captivity. It is wicked to pull that scripture today to try to get with your brother's widow.

precepts.text: If the man refused, the widow loosed his shoe and spat in his face before the elders, because he would not build up his brother's house.
precepts.point: What law is that going back to? That law goes back to Deuteronomy 25, the duty of the husband's brother: the widow of the dead does not marry without unto a stranger, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. This law was taught in full when it was read ahead at Ruth 1:6-9 in these notes: the firstborn carries the weight of the name, and the shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house.
precepts.why:
The law also dealt with the brother who refused. “And if the man like not to take his brother’s wife, then let his brother’s wife go up to the gate unto the elders, and say, My husband’s brother refuseth to raise up unto his brother a name in Israel, he will not perform the duty of my husband’s brother.”

If he stood to it before the elders, his brother's wife would “loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face, and shall answer and say, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother’s house. And his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.”

The shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house. That is the weight behind Boaz telling the kinsman that whoever buys the field must also take Ruth, the wife of the dead: the name of Mahlon had to be raised up upon his inheritance.

precepts.text: The firstborn is the might and the beginning of strength, the excellency of dignity and power; you want somebody to carry on your name.
precepts.point: What law is that going back to? That law goes back to Deuteronomy 25, the duty of the husband's brother: the widow of the dead does not marry without unto a stranger, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. This law was taught in full when it was read ahead at Ruth 1:6-9 in these notes: the firstborn carries the weight of the name, and the shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house.
precepts.why:
The firstborn carries the weight of the name. “Reuben, thou art my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, the excellency of dignity, and the excellency of power”.

The firstborn is the might and the beginning of strength, the excellency of dignity and power. You want somebody to carry on your name, and that is why the firstborn of Ruth would succeed in the name of Mahlon, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.

precepts.text: Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph; the birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel.
precepts.point: What law is that going back to? That law goes back to Deuteronomy 25, the duty of the husband's brother: the widow of the dead does not marry without unto a stranger, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. This law was taught in full when it was read ahead at Ruth 1:6-9 in these notes: the firstborn carries the weight of the name, and the shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house.
precepts.why:
“Now the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel, (for he was the firstborn; but, forasmuch as he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph the son of Israel: and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.”

Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph. The birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel. That is why Boaz would not let the field pass without the wife of the dead: the name of the dead had to be raised up upon his inheritance.

precepts.text: The loosed shoe was the testimony in Israel against him that would not build up his brother's house; his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.
precepts.point: You can read about that shoe back in Deuteronomy 25.
precepts.why:
The kinsman drew off his shoe, and that was the manner in former time in Israel, a testimony to confirm all things. You can read about that shoe back in Deuteronomy 25. “Then shall his brother’s wife come unto him in the presence of the elders, and loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face, and shall answer and say, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother’s house.”

“And his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.” The loosed shoe was the testimony in Israel against him that would not build up his brother's house. So when the kinsman told Boaz, Buy it for thee, and drew off his shoe, he was confirming before all that he gave up the redeeming to Boaz.

precepts.text: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: the law Boaz was exercising toward his dead kinsman's house.
precepts.point: What law is Boaz exercising in this? Love thy neighbour as thyself. That is what Boaz was putting into place and applying, and that is why he is mentioned in the scriptures.
precepts.why:
What law is Boaz exercising when he buys all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and takes Ruth to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance? “Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.”

Love thy neighbour as thyself. That is what Boaz was putting into place and applying toward his dead kinsman's house, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and that is why he is mentioned in the scriptures.

precepts.text: Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and Ruth was of Moab; their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews' language.
precepts.point: Why did Naomi take that child from Ruth the Moabitess? Because it is not the custom of Israel to allow a child to be raised up under the hand of a heathen. Although Ruth was used to keep Mahlon's name alive in Israel, and although she was brought in, she was a vessel; she did not have the same standing of rights as an Israelite woman, and she had no hand in raising the child. Naomi took it and raised it as her own, so that it could learn the ways of Israel.
precepts.why:
Why did Naomi take that child from Ruth the Moabitess? Because it is not the custom of Israel to allow a child to be raised up under the hand of a heathen. Nehemiah shows what happens when it is. “In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab: And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.”

Ruth was of Moab. A child's first teacher is the mother: she nurses him, he spends all his time with her, and he takes on her ways. So the children of those wives could not even speak the Jews' language. Although Ruth was used to keep Mahlon's name alive and was brought in, she was a vessel; she did not have the same standing of rights as an Israelite woman, and she had no hand in raising the child. Naomi took it immediately after it was born and raised it as her own, so that it could learn the ways of Israel. That is why the neighbours said, There is a son born to Naomi.

precepts.text: Salmon begat Booz of Rachab, and Booz begat Obed of Ruth, and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David the king; the same lineage runs on down to Christ.
precepts.point: We read that lineage in Matthew chapter 1: how David came about, how Solomon came about, ultimately down to Christ.
precepts.why:
Pharez is of Judah, so these generations are the lineage of Judah right down to the king, and we read the same lineage in Matthew chapter 1. “And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse; And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias”.

Salmon begat Boaz, Boaz begat Obed of Ruth, Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David the king. Matthew shows how David came about and how Solomon came about, and the same lineage runs on down to Christ.

precepts.text: Boaz raises up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that his name be not cut off from among his brethren; that is what the law was for.
precepts.point: He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living.

note.label: Mark 12: The Husbandmen, the Tribute, and the First Commandment

precepts.why:
The Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, build a question on the law Moses wrote: “If a man’s brother die, and leave his wife behind him, and leave no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.” Seven brethren, one wife, no seed; whose wife is she in the resurrection? “Do ye not therefore err, because ye know not the scriptures, neither the power of God?”

They did not know what that law was for. Boaz shows it: “Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place”. The law was for inheritance, so that a dead man's name and portion would not be put out of Israel. It has nothing to do with whose wife a woman is in the resurrection.

A woman is bound by that law while her husband lives, and “when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage”. In the resurrection there is no more dying, so there is no dead brother's name to raise up. “He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living”.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Pharez begat Hezron, Hezron begat Ram, Ram begat Amminadab, Amminadab begat Nahshon, Nahshon begat Salmon, Salmon begat Boaz, Boaz begat Obed, Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Raising up seed does not give a child two fathers; the record says Boaz begat Obed, not Mahlon, because Mahlon was dead.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Boaz went up to the gate, called the kinsman of whom he had spoken to turn aside and sit down, and took ten men of the elders of the city to sit with them.

Boaz laid the matter before the kinsman: Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land which was our brother Elimelech's. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it; but if not, tell me, for there is none to redeem it beside thee, and I am after thee. And the kinsman said, I will redeem it.

What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. Whoever took the land had to take the dead brother's wife with it; Ruth the Moabitess came along as a parcel of the land, to keep the name of Mahlon alive.

What law is that going back to? That law goes back to Deuteronomy 25, the duty of the husband's brother: the widow of the dead does not marry without unto a stranger, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. This law was taught in full when it was read ahead at Ruth 1:6-9 in these notes: the firstborn carries the weight of the name, and the shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house.

Notice the bottom of verse 5: to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. This law applies to inheritance; it went into the law of land being passed down. It does not apply today: your husband dying does not mean his brother now has to go in unto you and raise up children, because that duty was due to the law of inheritance, and Israel has no land inheritance in this captivity. It is wicked to pull that scripture today to try to get with your brother's widow.

The kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself, for I cannot redeem it. In other words, I already have kids in the way; I cannot do it, I am not doing it.

Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing: for to confirm all things, a man plucked off his shoe and gave it to his neighbour, and this was a testimony in Israel. So the kinsman said unto Boaz, Buy it for thee, and he drew off his shoe.

Boaz said unto the elders and unto all the people, Ye are witnesses this day that I have bought all that was Elimelech's, and all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, of the hand of Naomi; moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place.

All the people that were in the gate and the elders said, We are witnesses. They blessed the marriage: the Lord make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel; and let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Judah, of the seed which the Lord shall give thee of this young woman.
So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife; and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.

The women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the Lord, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel; he shall be unto thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him.

Why did Naomi take that child from Ruth the Moabitess? Because it is not the custom of Israel to allow a child to be raised up under the hand of a heathen. Although Ruth was used to keep Mahlon's name alive in Israel, and although she was brought in, she was a vessel; she did not have the same standing of rights as an Israelite woman, and she had no hand in raising the child. Naomi took it and raised it as her own, so that it could learn the ways of Israel.

Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it; and the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

A child's first teacher is the mother: she is the one who nurses him, he spends all his time with her, and he takes on her ways. So what Naomi did in the spirit, she did immediately after that child was born: she took it and raised it as her own. Notice the neighbours said, There is a son born to Naomi; Naomi did not bear that son, Ruth did, but she took it as her own.

Now these are the generations of Pharez: Pharez is of Judah, so this is the lineage of Judah, how they came about right down to the king. Pharez begat Hezron, and Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab, and Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon, and Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.
